name: Luc Colgrove
occupation: Entrepreneur; built a Casper sound and event production company (self-reported in Oil City News coverage)
background: Luc Colgrove is a lifelong Casper resident. Oil City News, in a May 1, 2026 announcement of his House District 57 campaign, described him as a Casper entrepreneur and community organizer who maintains a “Natrona's Gadfly” social media presence.

That Oil City News report quoted him as saying he built a local sound and event production company that grew to more than $750,000 in annual sales. It also reported that he previously served as vice president of the board for the Rock the Block summer concert series and has organized community cleanups in the Old Yellowstone District.
In WyoFile's 2026 election guide he wrote that he is a lifelong Casper resident and a stepdad to three girls, and that his family was forced to move during a market crash.

positions.topic: What are the biggest challenges and opportunities facing Wyoming today? As a legislator, how would you address them?
positions.text: We have an opportunity to grow in several ways across the state. First, our kids are leaving, schools are being cut. Next, healthcare in Wyoming is struggling, from physical to mental wellbeing, and even addiction. …

positions.topic: We asked WyoFile readers to rank issues that are important to them, and healthcare costs and access topped the list. What can the Legislature do to make healthcare more affordable and accessible to Wyomingites?
positions.text: Wyoming already sees a shortage of doctors in nearly every county across the state. While we’ve seen that shortage, many of these communities have seen one or two specific resources take over where local doctors used to serve. …

positions.topic: Do you support efforts to sell or transfer public land in Wyoming? How do you plan to ensure that state and federal land is managed in the best interest of the people of Wyoming?
positions.text: I want to be very clear here; I grew up here in Wyoming. I’ve hunted and fished these lands religiously since I was a child. These are also the same lands I take my children to learn, play, and grow. I appreciate the resources, labor, and love that are dedicated to caring for our land daily. …

positions.topic: No two Wyoming counties are the same when it comes to how they generate revenue. As a legislator, how would you approach the public's desire for property tax relief with local revenue needs?
positions.text: I believe that the public deserves tax relief, but I’m not sure we’re approaching it the right way. Property tax relief specifically helps people who own property. Roughly a quarter of all Wyoming families are renters. …

positions.topic: What role, if any, should the Wyoming Legislature play in economic development?
positions.text: I believe the Legislature's role in economic development should be to create the conditions for private industry to thrive, not to run or ruin it. The film industry is a perfect example. …

positions.topic: Explain your values when it comes to campaign donations. Does Wyoming's system for monitoring campaign donations and expenditures need reform?
positions.text: I believe in transparency for campaign donations. I’m not sure if I think the system needs reform at this time, but if I were to support any reform, it would be with ease of access for the voter, while not creating a barrier for potential candidates, at the front of my mind.
